localContext: Evanston’s position along Lake Michigan exposes garage door systems to harsh conditions. Lake-effect snow, strong winds, and airborne moisture affect moving parts. Salt air from winter road treatments and the lake itself accelerates corrosion on hinges, cables, and bottom seals. This increased friction and resistance makes garage door openers work harder. Over time, this strain can damage drive gears, belts, or logic boards. Homes in the Ridge Historic District or South Evanston often feature original detached garages. These older structures, common in the Northwestern campus area, house aged opener systems. Their components are more susceptible to these environmental factors, leading to premature failure of motors, sensors, and trolleys.

problemSigns.sign: Opener hums, door does not move
problemSigns.detail: The motor runs, but the door remains stationary. This often points to a stripped drive gear.

problemSigns.sign: Door reverses before touching the floor
problemSigns.detail: The door detects an obstruction too early. Safety sensor alignment or damage is often the cause.
The opener does not react to commands from remotes or the wall console. Logic board failure or wiring issues can be at fault.
The infrared beam is interrupted or misaligned. This prevents the door from closing fully.

problemSigns.sign: Trolley moves, but door stays down
problemSigns.detail: The carriage detaches from the door. This indicates a broken or disengaged trolley carriage.
